document_title: The State Flew the Kuskokwim. An AI Prospector Arrived.
post_copy:
On June 23rd, 2024, four fixed-wing aircraft began flying the Kuskokwim for the state's McGrath survey.
Lines ran 400 meters apart and about 100 meters up.

Federal Earth MRI grants paid for McGrath and its data is a free download. Four more state surveys came out this year.

On October 20th Geomorphic AI formed Golden Dyke Exploration in Alaska. Geomorphic calls itself an AI-driven minerals prospect generator that packages targets and keeps an interest. It hasn't said whether it uses these surveys.

One real McGrath flight line's magnetic profile, a map and a card of five state surveys, the Ganes Creek radiometrics printed with three grant numbers, and an empty pocket for a first Alaska property, none named yet.

The state says the data will promote resource exploration. Does packaging targets for others to drill count as that exploration?

#EarthMRI #Geophysics #AlaskaMining

slides.headline: 86,319 km of public survey lines. Now an AI prospector.
On October 20th, an AI prospect generator set up in Alaska.
slides.body: Geomorphic AI formed Golden Dyke Exploration LLC, a wholly owned Alaska subsidiary. Its release says new state airborne surveys extend decades of USGS and state mapping. It names no Alaska property yet.

slides.headline: It packages the target, not the drill.
slides.body: Geomorphic says its role is to generate and package targets, then advance them through joint ventures and earn-ins while keeping an interest. It doesn't fund or operate drilling. It hasn't said whether it uses these surveys.
labels: A 20 KM SQUARE OF THE PUBLIC MCGRATH FIELD. NOT A TARGET.

slides.headline: Lines 400 meters apart, about 100 meters up.
slides.body: Four fixed-wing aircraft flew McGrath over two summers, 86,319 line kilometers in all. A cesium sensor read the rock's magnetism. Two gamma-ray spectrometers read its radiation.
labels: THE SURVEY GRID IN SECTION, 5X VERTICAL

slides.headline: The McGrath block, read every 400 meters.
labels: MAGNETIC FIELD AS COLOR ON THE SURVEY'S OWN TERRAIN. ILLUSTRATIVE VIEW, 2.5X RELIEF.

slides.headline: Five surveys, one scale.
labels: OUTLINES AT ONE SCALE. BARS IN LINE KILOMETERS.

slides.headline: Paid for by Earth MRI. Free to download.
slides.body: Federal Earth MRI grants paid for the flying. The state posts the data under an open end-user license. DGGS says it will promote resource exploration of the central Kuskokwim.
labels: EARTH MRI GRANTS FOR MCGRATH, GANES CREEK AND ANIAK
PRINTED AT RIGHT, GANES CREEK RADIOMETRICS, POTASSIUM, THORIUM, URANIUM

slides.headline: Open input. Private output.
slides.body: The flying, the grids and the license are public. A packaged target moves through private deals, with an interest kept. Geomorphic has named no Alaska property yet.
labels: FIRST ALASKA PROPERTY NONE NAMED YET

slides.headline: Should a target built on public surveys say which ones it used?

aftercare: Post when it suits your cadence. The strongest slots are Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, so today (Thursday October 22nd) or next Tuesday morning. The October 20th news gets older each day it waits.
Paste the sources block as the first comment within 60 seconds of posting. Paste it as plain text so every raw URL stays visible.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. If anyone asks whether Geomorphic used these surveys, the only sourced answer is that it hasn't said (North of 60 Mining News, October 21st).
After 48 hours, record saves, comments and reposts, and note which slide people quote (the card on 06 or the ask on 09) for the instincts ledger.
